Dear YJ.

Please be informed that last week meeting memo for SINOKOR 2800TEU Container carrier lashing issue as follow.

Item No1 : KR Lashing calculation result comparison with BV result. BV’s explanation:

**KPO explanation :** The results from KR and BV may differ depending on the calculation parameters listed below.  

- Ship motion acceleration based on Class rules.
- On deck container stack COG.
- Twistlocks (Manual/ Semi-automatic/Fully automatic) horizontal and vertical gap. / Horizontal gap : 5mm, Vertical gap 12mm ~ 20mm.

In particular, the third item can have a significant impact on the calculation results, so it is necessary to verify which value was applied in KR’s calculation.

Item No.2 : If the lashing bridge is installed on a SINOKOR vessels, how should any non-compliance with the CSS Code be addressed?

**KPO explanation :** Compliance with the exact CSS code requirements can only be assessed once detailed lashing bridge drawings are available and reviewed.

Any identified non-compliance items must be evaluated on a case-by-case basis. For clear deviations from CSS Code requirements. An exemption from the Liberia Flag will need to be obtained.

For next meeting, the lashing calculation results in between KR and BV will be compared using same twistlocks gap (horizontal/vertical). In addition, BV is requested to calculate and provide the upper deck deflection at Bay38.   

Best Regards

Dear Christophe,

Please refer to below our observation regarding the RSSA.

The LASHING-RSSA notation was discussed and agreed in between KPO and DA Hull on 10 Feb. 2026 following SINKOR’s continued complaints after ship’s delivery regarding container loadability.

The affected vessels are listed below.

|   |   |   |
|---|---|---|
|Ship|Hull No|Delivery|
|42639Y  -  QINGDAO VOYAGER|4225|8-May-2024|
|42640A  -  TIANJIN VOYAGER|4226|25-July-2024|
|42641B  -  NINGBO VOYAGER|4227|10-Sep-2024|
|42642C  -  LAEM CHABANG VOYAGER|4228|16-Oct-2024|

It was concluded that applying the RSSA would enable an increase in on‑deck container loading capacity for the subject vessels, compared with the currently assigned LASHING‑WW notation.

Based on this technical clarification and SINOKOR’s expressed concerns, the LASHING‑RSSA option was presented to the SINOKOR shipowner on 12 Feb. 2026, taking into account the operating routes of the subject vessels.

This was limited to explaining the available improvement option and did not constitute a proposal for any additional scope.

Subsequently, the SINOKOR requested information regarding the BV approval cost and required timeline, which is currently under internal review.

Once the BV approval fee is confirmed, DA Hull will proceed with the review of the LASHING‑RSSA notation (Routes 16, 17, and 18) in accordance with SINOKOR’s request.

Please let us know if you require any further clarification.

Best regards,

Young-Jun (YJ)

Dear All,

First for Mr. Han, I am not HO Lashing expert, I am HO DA Hull manager, in charge of management of the team for design approval of the structure of the units and for qualification and quality of LPOs for Hull topic.

**1 – Context**

Regarding the context, note that we did not make any mistake during approval and followed rule approach & design input.

Designer is in charge of defining the input data for operation and the operational limitation and is fully responsible of this. In this case, designer is HMD. Designer of lashing himself (SEC) confirmed that the agreement between those inputs datas was made between Owner & designer. SEC did full design of lashing system based on those inputs and we checked it based on the same input. It is aligned with Rules.

**2 – Proposal**

Regarding the request to waive the fees, please note that our normal price internal would have been 35010 euros internal for this scope. This was sent by François some weeks ago. This is the price we invoice to all clients, and we do not make profit on it.

We agreed a reduction to 23419 euros internal (26931 euros external) which is a huge fee reduction on which we are already in deficit from our side.

I understand for commercial reason, you want us to reduce even more the price and therefore to increase the loss and deficit to invest on local client.

As said in answer from Francois to you dated 07/04/2026, we can accept to reduce it more if BV Korea accept to share with us the additional cost on the budget.

_“__In case you expect to go further as a commercial gesture towards you client, we may share the commercial effort between DA and BV Korea to limit the negative impact of this case on our budget.”_

You did not answer to this email so we could not discuss more if there was a need for such effort. In such situation, normal process would be to share additional reduction of fees by 50% with BV Korea.

**3 – Action Plan**

- Regarding the fee proposal, see my answer above.
- Regarding the request to have a formal presentation on lashing, we can organize a formal presentation on Lashing, Lashing RSSA without any issue. Presentation would be done by J. Skadins in such case, HO formal expert on lashing.

Could you please provide your inputs?

Best regards

Guillaume BROCHET

DA Hull manager

**Subject:** Sinokor – Lashing Claim Update & Consideration for RSSA fee

Dear Mr. Vaes,

I would like to report a full update on the ongoing lashing claim issue involving Sinokor, along with a strategic proposal to strengthen our commercial position as we navigate this situation.

# 1. Background

Sinokor has been experiencing serious operational difficulties with 2,800 TEU vessels built at Hyundai Mipo Dockyard (HMD) with BV class. Due to the wider-than-standard hull design of these vessels, lashing forces under full load conditions exceed the permissible limits. As a result, despite their rated capacity of 2,800 TEU, the actual number of containers that can be safely loaded is only in the low 2,000s, causing significant cargo revenue loss for the client.

# 2. Current Situation

Sinokor holds HMD primarily responsible for this issue, given that HMD contracted directly with the lashing plan provider (GLS) and built the vessels accordingly. Sinokor is preparing to file a formal claim against HMD for approximately KRW 7 billion. BV is not a party to this claim and remains technically neutral.

That said, Sinokor has expressed dissatisfaction with BV as well, given that the problems arose despite loading being carried out in accordance with the Cargo Securing Manual (CSM) and lashing program approved by BV. This dissatisfaction, while separate from any legal liability, represents a relationship-level concern that must be addressed.

To mitigate the lashing force issue, BV has proposed the application of the RSSA (Reduced Ship Motions Acceleration) notation to the four vessels (HMD Hull Nos. 4225–4228). KPO presented Sinokor yesterday with a revised quote of EUR 26,931 — a reduction of approximately 23% from the original BV Paris estimate of EUR 35,010. However, Sinokor has pushed back, citing a lack of reference data on the expected improvement in lashing forces following RSSA application, and is strongly requesting that the service be provided at no charge.

# 3. Key Risks

Sinokor is currently advancing plans to order four 5,000 TEU newbuildings at a Chinese shipyard, with the shipyard selection process now underway. A broker of KR (Korean Register) background operating in China has been maintaining close contact with Sinokor’s senior management and is actively lobbying for KR adoption during the shipyard selection process. In addition, a KR-affiliated technical advisor is stationed at Sinokor and is encouraging the selection of KR for newbuilding orders. Should BV respond passively or maintain its position on the RSSA fee of EUR 26,931, there is a very high risk of losing this newbuilding project to KR. Furthermore, this case could become a key reason for the technical advisor overseeing future newbuilding orders to steer Sinokor away from BV.

# 4. Proposal

To turn this situation into a strategic opportunity, I kindly request your review and approval to submit a request to HQ for a full waiver of the RSSA fee of **EUR 26,931 (covering four vessels, Routes 16, 17 & 18)**. While BV bears no legal liability in this matter, proactively absorbing this cost would serve as a strategic commercial investment — one that addresses the client’s frustration and demonstrates BV’s commitment to a genuine partnership.

# 5. Action Plan

Subject to your approval, the following actions will be taken:

- Submit a formal request to DA for the RSSA fee waiver
- Submit a formal request to DA for a technical seminar on “Container General & Lashing.” BV Paris lashing expert Guillaume Brochet will be requested as the presenter. The seminar will be held in a hybrid format, with HQ (Paris) joining online and KPO (Busan) hosting an in-person session, to maximize attendance and engagement from Sinokor’s management team.

# 6. Expected Outcome

By combining the RSSA fee waiver with a technical seminar led by a leading BV expert, we can position BV as a proactive partner that voluntarily supports Sinokor through both its technical and financial challenges. This approach will help neutralize the influence of the KR broker and the KR-affiliated technical advisor stationed at Sinokor, and strengthen the grounds and confidence for Sinokor to select BV for its upcoming newbuilding orders.

I would appreciate your review and comment. 

**_Best Regards,_**
